properties.decision:
`release_without_manifest` is raised at severity 0.85, above `reflow2_check`'s default `--gap-threshold` of 0.8, so a Release that is pinned to an epoch, deployed, and includes nothing FAILS the gate rather than appearing as a note.

It joins the band of findings that say the design asserts something untrue — failing_verification 0.80, kpp_contradicted 0.85, kpp_unbound 0.90, kpp_breached 0.95 — rather than the band below it, which holds questions waiting for a human. Its sibling `release_without_epoch` stays at 0.6 and stays a question: WHICH epoch a release belongs to is a judgement, and nothing false has been asserted by the edge's absence.

A genuinely contentless release — a re-tag, a docs-only republish — remains a real state. It is red until somebody acknowledges it with a reason on the record, never red forever.

DISTINCT FROM the requirement it settles a question about: that says the state shall be REPORTED, and would be satisfied by a detector of any severity. This says how loud the report is, which is a separate choice with its own cost — a red build on a contentless release — and could be reversed without touching the requirement at all.
properties.name: DECIDED — a published release recording that it shipped nothing stops the build
properties.rationale:
ANTHONY'S CALL, 2026-08-21, asked as a direct choice between stopping the build, staying a note at 0.65, and expressing it as a DesignRule carrying enforcement. He chose to stop the build.

THE EVIDENCE PUT TO HIM, AND IT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT: a note was already demonstrably not enough. The v0.38.0 cut passed `reflow2_check` GREEN with 96 notes scrolling past it, and that is exactly how a tag was pushed, built, published and asset-verified over an empty manifest. A finding nobody is made to read is not a finding.

THE COST WAS STATED BEFORE HE CHOSE: a release that really did ship no new content will red-build until acknowledged, which is one call with his reason attached.

WHY NOT THE DESIGNRULE ROUTE, which was offered and not taken: it is the cleaner separation of "how bad" from "does CI fail", and it would have needed checking that the rule actually reaches `reflow2_check`. Left on the table rather than refuted — if severity ever has to be tuned for a reason unrelated to CI, that is the route back.

THE NUMBER IS NOT TUNED TO THE THRESHOLD. 0.85 sits above 0.80 with room, deliberately, so raising `--gap-threshold` one notch does not silently drop the rule out of the gate — the failure mode this whole line of work exists to prevent.
